ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a chemical structure with two curved arrows; ignore these arrows according to the problem statement. In the retained chemical figure, the central carbon atom is connected to two substituent labels R1 and R2, and forms a double bond with N; N is then connected to an oxygen labeled OH2 and bearing a positive charge. Reasoning: Replace both substituents R1 and R2 with the SMILES wildcard *. Therefore the central carbon is written as connected to one *, connected to another * in branch form, and at the same time double-bonded to N; N is single-bonded to the protonated oxygen [OH2+]. The corresponding SMILES is *C(*)=N[OH2+].

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a chemical graph rather than a reaction mechanism: ignore the curved electron-flow arrows and keep only atoms, labels, charges, and bonds. Replace the two substituents labeled R1 and R2 on the central carbon by wildcard atoms. Encode the central carbon as bonded to one wildcard, branched to the second wildcard, double-bonded to N, and N single-bonded to protonated oxygen `[OH2+]`, yielding `*C(*)=N[OH2+]`.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中是一个化学结构，带有两条弯曲箭头；按题意忽略这些箭头。保留的化学图形中，中心碳原子连接两个取代基标签 R1 和 R2，并与 N 形成双键；N 再与标注为 OH2 且带正电荷的氧相连。推理：将 R1 和 R2 两个取代基都替换为 SMILES 通配符 *。因此中心碳写作与一个 * 相连，并以分支形式连接另一个 *，同时双键连接 N；N 单键连接质子化氧 [OH2+]。对应 SMILES 为 *C(*)=N[OH2+]。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct structure-to-SMILES route: identify the atom connectivity in the drawing while explicitly discarding the curved arrows, then encode that graph in SMILES. With this problem there is essentially one honest solution path, so the method is not intended to be strongly distinct from alternatives.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the skeletal structure: a central carbon is single-bonded to two substituent groups labeled R1 and R2, double-bonded to nitrogen, and that nitrogen is single-bonded to an O bearing two hydrogens and a positive charge. Curved arrows are visible but should not be treated as bonds or atoms.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the prompt instruction that the requested output is a SMILES expression and that arrows in the transition-state drawing must be ignored.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use SMILES conventions: generic R groups can be represented as wildcard atoms `*`; single bonds may be omitted; a C=N double bond is written with `=`; a positively charged oxygen with two hydrogens attached through oxygen is bracketed as `[OH2+]`. Combine the connectivity as wildcard–carbon–wildcard with `=N[OH2+]`.
